clue.text: Mean shade one must overlook

parts.note: mean in the slang sense of excellent, as in 'plays a mean guitar'
a visor shades the eyes

explanation.surface: A spiteful shade or ghost that someone has to put up with or ignore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like nastiness but is the slang for excellent; 'overlook' is used in its sense of oversee, not ignore.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook can mean to oversee, so a person whose job is overseeing others is one who must overlook.

clue.text: Special salad spinner

parts.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
rocket is a peppery salad leaf (arugula)

explanation.surface: A special gadget for drying salad leaves by spinning them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salad spinner' reads as one kitchen gadget, but the split falls between them: salad is the leaf, spinner the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed wheel that turns to drive a chain or film is something that rotates, a spinner.

clue.text: Cream ran out of it

parts.note: the cream of something is the pick, the best of it
ran a company or team, i.e. led it

explanation.surface: The cream was used up: someone ran out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran out of it' reads as a phrase about running short, but it splits after 'ran', and 'out of it' is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is informal for drunk, and being out of it is likewise slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: Support restriction on tough setter?

parts.note: a rein is a restraint or check
on in the sense of in favour of, as in 'I'm for it'
cement sets hard

explanation.surface: Backing a restriction placed on a harsh crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' suggests the crossword compiler, but here it is something that sets: a building material that hardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforcement is extra strengthening or backup, which is support for a structure or force.

clue.text: International footballer last in coconut shy

parts.note: INT is the standard abbreviation for international
a player for a club called Rovers, such as Bristol Rovers or Tranmere Rovers

indicators.note: last picks out only the closing letter of the word that follows

parts.note: closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A footballer capped for his country comes last at the fairground coconut shy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coconut shy' is a fairground stall where balls are thrown at coconuts; here 'shy' is cut off and stands alone as the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is a reserved, inward-looking person, and shy is the matching adjective describing that temperament.

clue.text: Heading off row, allowed youth in parliament

indicators.note: the head of the following word comes off, so its opening letter is lost

parts.note: row without its first letter
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A young MP walks out after a row, having been allowed into the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: A parliament is the collective noun for owls, so a youngster in one is a baby owl, not a young politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament is the collective noun for a group of owls, so a young bird in such a group is a juvenile owl.

clue.text: Small device for recording fiddle

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a cam is a camera, as in webcam or bodycam

explanation.surface: A tiny gadget used to make a recording of a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle in the informal sense is a swindle or con, which is what a scam is.

clue.text: My expert arrangement for the wedding party

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
a sage is a wise or expert person

explanation.surface: Someone boasting that they arranged things for the wedding guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is an exclamation of surprise; 'arrangement' suggests planning, though it means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bunch of flowers pinned to the clothes is a floral arrangement typically worn by members of a bridal party.

clue.text: Bass-drinking fellow beginning to crave wine

indicators.note: someone drinking takes something inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: a fellow is a man, a male
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word means just its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man drinking Bass beer starts to long for wine instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Bass is a well-known British brand of ale, so 'Bass-drinking' reads as beer-drinking; here it is just the musical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Malbec is a red grape variety and the red wine made from it, associated especially with Argentina.

clue.text: Getting on with church, then one pint

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
CE is the Church of England
I is the Roman numeral one
PT is the abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: Someone ageing, going to church, then having a pint afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' reads as growing old, but the definition is 'Getting' alone, and 'on' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipt in its formal sense is the act of receiving, as in 'on receipt of payment', which is getting something.

clue.text: Ample smear coats painter

indicators.note: a coat goes all round something, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a smear is a damaging false statement, a libel
RA is a Royal Academician, the standard crossword painter

explanation.surface: A generous smear of paint coats the decorator.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures paint on a painter, but smear means slander here.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping, which is the same as ample.

clue.text: Basic seats on vacation unless flying this?

definitions.text: Basic seats on vacation unless flying this?

indicators.note: flying suggests letters scattered about and landing in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: vacating a word empties it, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the word emptied of its middle
taken as written

explanation.surface: Economy seats are what you get on holiday, unless you fly in a pricier cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a definition: the cabin you fly in to avoid basic seats on a holiday flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle cabin on an airliner is the obvious alternative to cramped economy seating for travellers who can afford it.

clue.text: Conservative grey hairdo finally shaven flat, this heralds cooler times

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
grey-haired, i.e. old
a 'fro is a short form of afro

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of each of the two words after it

parts.note: closing letters of both words

explanation.surface: A grey-haired Tory has his hair cut flat, signalling a chillier era ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fro is an accepted informal shortening of afro.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold front is the leading edge of a cold air mass in weather forecasting, which brings a drop in temperature.

clue.text: Watch bit of EastEnders after Red Dwarf?

parts.note: a red dwarf is a small cool type of star; the question mark flags an example

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is a single letter, its first

parts.note: opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Viewing a clip of the BBC soap EastEnders after the sci-fi sitcom Red Dwarf.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Dwarf is a British sci-fi sitcom and EastEnders a BBC soap opera, so the clue reads as a TV schedule; the dwarf is astronomy.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch someone intently is to gaze at them fixedly, which is to stare.

clue.text: Bush Senior

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shrub bearing elderflowers and berries
second meaning: older, of greater age

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests George Bush Senior, the US president; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a common shrub of the genus Sambucus and also means an older person or senior figure.

clue.text: Scrap divorcee joke, perhaps, after pushback?

parts.note: a divorcee is someone's ex
a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: pushing something back sends it the other way, so the word runs right to left

parts.note: perhaps signals an example, eg

explanation.surface: Drop a joke about a former spouse after it meets resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To expunge is to erase or remove completely, which is to scrap something.

clue.text: Trunk for higher-up coming around Channel Islands

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: coming around something means going all the way round it, enclosing it

parts.note: a boss is someone higher up
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A storage chest for a senior manager who is visiting Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are the British crown dependencies off Normandy, such as Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's trunk is its long flexible nose, which is a proboscis.

clue.text: Dark web gets savage on the fringes

indicators.note: one word sits on the fringes of another, on both sides of it

parts.note: a brute is a savage
a net is a web, or the web is the Net

explanation.surface: The dark web lets savage characters lurk at its margins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark web' reads as one phrase, but 'Dark' is the definition and 'web' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark-haired woman is a brunette, so the noun names someone with dark hair; the definition works as a noun sense of dark-haired.

clue.text: Great player, most are awful

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Only a few performers are truly great; most are dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician or conductor, a virtuoso performer.

clue.text: Consider leaving time to go between parties?

indicators.note: the abbreviation that is leaving departs from the word it was in

parts.note: to meditate on something is to consider it
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Think about skipping the time spent hopping between social events.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Ts goes; either gives the same result.
explanation.definitionFit: To mediate is to act as a go-between in a dispute, intervening between two sides to reach agreement.

clue.text: Direct source of meat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to guide or point the way
second meaning: a castrated bull reared for beef

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a farm shop selling straight from the producer; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning to guide a course and a noun for a bullock raised for its beef.

clue.text: The best story about getting high?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so everything before it runs backwards

parts.note: the best is number one, No 1, with the 1 read as I
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: The finest tale about taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'getting high' is a stretch for a feeling: high spirits, not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great joy, a sense of being on a high, so 'getting high' is a playful gloss on it.

clue.text: What's above Americans? Roughly nothing

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly
nada is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Asking what ranks higher than Americans, and answering that very little does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Above' sounds like superiority, but it is geography: the country lying north of the United States on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: The country borders the United States to the north, so on a map it sits above Americans.

clue.text: Throw bat in table-tennis when losing lead

indicators.note: losing the lead means the front letter is dropped

parts.note: a table-tennis bat is called a paddle

explanation.surface: A player hurls the bat in a ping-pong match after falling behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' looks like hurling the bat, but it means to confuse, as in 'the question threw me'.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to disconcert them, and to addle is likewise to muddle or confuse.

clue.text: Wolves are top here and Ohio FC struggles

indicators.note: a struggle throws things into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: League table news: Wolverhampton Wanderers lead while an Ohio football club struggles.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club, so 'top' suggests a league table; really it is predators at the top of an ecological hierarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: In an ecosystem's feeding hierarchy, wolves are apex predators, so they sit at the top of this sequence of eaters and eaten.

clue.text: Sacrifice of calf or goat

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the letters come from inside the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: An offering of a young cow or a goat at an altar.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to give it up or do without it, which is to sacrifice it.

clue.text: Plug fitting over another's end

parts.note: fitting in the sense of adjusting to suit, making fit
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the end of a word is just its closing letter

parts.note: closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fitting a plug over the end of someone else's cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug fitting' reads as one electrical phrase, but only 'Plug' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel converter that lets one kind of plug go into a different socket is itself a kind of plug.

clue.text: Ancient vehicle lad almost brought to rave

indicators.note: almost all of the word means its final letter is cut off

parts.note: a chap, without its last letter
a riot is a wild party or uproar, like a rave

explanation.surface: An old car that a young man nearly drove to an all-night party.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn war or racing car of antiquity, as in Ben-Hur, is the classic ancient vehicle.

clue.text: Agreed noodle dish blows away the starter

indicators.note: blowing away the starter removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: ramen is a Japanese noodle soup

explanation.surface: Everyone concurs that the noodle soup outshines the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course, which fits the food picture, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said to express assent, so as an interjection it means 'so be it', that is, agreed.

clue.text: Oh no, trustees being sued regularly given judgment

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every second letter

parts.note: every second letter, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Dismay as the trustees face a lawsuit and a court ruling is handed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judgment' suggests a court verdict, fitting the lawsuit; it means good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse sense is shrewd practical wisdom, the sound judgment of a sensible person.
